_comment: Songs before 1929, easy rags and classical themes, own arrangements (L1 plan, Task 12). Specs and references: tools/arrangements/songs.py. One main candidate was rejected (see 'rejected') and replaced by the spare in-the-good-old-summertime.

pieces.title: Camptown Races
pieces.tempoSource: editorial: the 1852 Benteen edition marks Moderato without a metronome mark; with the note values doubled, quarter = 100 (eighth = 100 in the original 2/4)
pieces.levelNote: Level 1: right hand in C position (C4 to G4) with the A as its one extension, single notes; left hand whole and half notes on C, F and G in one position (C3 to G3), open fifths at the cadences; no published syllabus placement exists for this arrangement; heuristic proposes 1 (score 1.24)
pieces.notes: Original title 'Gwine to Run All Night' (F. D. Benteen, Baltimore, 1850). The verse only, arranged in C major (the source is in D major) with the note values doubled; the chorus climbs to the upper octave and is left out.

reference.description: Wikisource transcription of the first edition (Benteen, 1850), solo voice of the verse, D major; checked against the 1852 Benteen guitar edition (Library of Congress scan on Wikimedia Commons, File:Camptownraces.gif)

pieces.title: Oh! Susanna
pieces.tempoSource: editorial: the 1848 edition marks Allegretto without a metronome mark; with the note values doubled, quarter = 108 is about half the song's usual speed, a beginner pace
pieces.levelNote: Level 1: right hand in G position (G4 to D5) with the E as its one extension, single notes; left hand whole and half notes on G, C and D (G2 to D3) with open fifths; no published syllabus placement exists for this arrangement; heuristic proposes 2 (score 2.21), just over the first cut (1.76) because of the 24 bars and the open fifths
pieces.notes: Verse 1 and the chorus, played once, in the source's key of G major with the note values doubled; the dotted eighth-sixteenth pairs are straightened.

reference.description: Wikisource transcription of an 1848 edition (plate 1427), voice and chorus Air, G major; checked against Duke University's copy of the same plate (Historic American Sheet Music n1329)

pieces.title: Long, Long Ago
pieces.tempoSource: editorial: the 1839 Cramer edition marks 'With feeling' without a metronome mark; quarter = 84
pieces.levelNote: Level 1: right hand in F position (F4 to C5) with the D as its one extension, single notes; left hand open fifths and single notes from F2 to C3; no published syllabus placement exists for this arrangement; heuristic proposes 2 (score 2.46), raised by the open fifths in the left hand
pieces.notes: Written in 1833; the earliest edition found is Cramer, Addison & Beale's (London), advertised in February 1839, a few weeks before Bayly's death. The first eight bars only (the A section, ending on the tonic), in the source's key of F major; the middle section drops to C4 and is left out.

reference.description: Scan of the Cramer, Addison & Beale edition (London, 1839; Internet Archive BaylyLongLongAgo1839Sheetmusic), voice, bars 1-8, F major

pieces.title: Little Brown Jug
pieces.tempoSource: editorial: the 1869 edition marks Allegretto without a metronome mark; with the note values doubled, quarter = 108
pieces.levelNote: Level 1: right hand in G position (G4 to D5) with the E as its one extension, single notes; left hand whole and half notes from C3 to G3; no published syllabus placement exists for this arrangement; heuristic proposes 1 (score 1.27)
pieces.notes: Published under the pen name 'Eastburn'. The chorus only ('Ha, ha, ha, you and me'), in the source's key of C major with the note values doubled; the verse reaches down to E4 and is left out.

reference.description: Scan of the J. E. Winner edition (Philadelphia, 1869; Lilly Library, Indiana University), Air of the chorus, C major

pieces.title: Daisy Bell (A Bicycle Built for Two)
pieces.tempoSource: editorial: the 1893 edition marks the chorus 'A little faster' without a metronome mark; quarter = 120 follows the playback tempo of the Wikisource transcription of that edition
pieces.levelNote: Level 2: right hand single notes moving between D4 and D5 in G major; left hand waltz bass, a bass note and a two-note chord; no published syllabus placement exists for this arrangement; heuristic proposes 3 (score 4.73), raised by the waltz chords (chord share 0.67), which the heuristic overrates as it does for the core arrangements of Amazing Grace and Greensleeves
pieces.notes: Harry Dacre was the pen name of Frank Dean. The chorus only ('Daisy, Daisy, give me your answer do'), in the source's key of G major, with a waltz bass.

reference.description: Wikisource transcription of the 1893 New York printing (Internet Archive daisybell00harr), voice of the chorus, G major

pieces.title: In the Good Old Summer Time
pieces.tempoSource: editorial: the 1902 edition gives no metronome mark; quarter = 120, an easy waltz
pieces.levelNote: Level 2: right hand single notes moving between D4 and D5 in B-flat major; left hand waltz bass, a bass note and a two-note chord; no published syllabus placement exists for this arrangement; heuristic proposes 3 (score 5.07), raised by the waltz chords (chord share 0.67) and the two flats
pieces.notes: A spare of the L1 plan, used in place of maple-leaf-rag-easy (see 'rejected'). Words by Ren Shields (1868-1913), which are not printed. The chorus only, once with its second ending, in the source's key of B-flat major, with a waltz bass.

reference.description: Scan of the Howley, Haviland & Dresser edition (New York, 1902; University of Illinois Chicago Library, SMC_0016_0080), voice of the chorus, B-flat major

pieces.title: The Entertainer, A strain (simplified)
pieces.tempoSource: editorial: Joplin marks 'Not fast'; the library's engraving plays quarter = 72 in 2/4, and with the note values doubled quarter = 100 is a little slower, for a level-2 player
pieces.levelNote: Level 2: right hand the single-line melody from D4 to E5 with Joplin's chromatic pickups; left hand a bass note and a two-note chord on alternate beats; no published syllabus placement exists for this arrangement; heuristic proposes 3 (score 7.84), raised by the stride bass's leaps and position shifts; kept at 2 because each hand repeats a few shapes at a slow tempo
pieces.notes: The first strain (A strain) of The Entertainer as a single melody line over a simplified stride bass, in the original key of C major with the note values doubled. The library also has the complete rag (joplin-the-entertainer).

reference.description: The library's core engraving (content/scores/joplin-the-entertainer.musicxml, Mutopia 263, after the 1902 edition): melody line of the A strain, bars 4-20, C major

pieces.title: Theme from the "Surprise" Symphony
pieces.tempoSource: the reference score's Andante mark, eighth = 110, that is quarter = 55
pieces.levelNote: Level 2: right hand the violin theme from G3 to C5 in C major, single notes with two octave drops; left hand a bass note and a two-note chord per bar; no published syllabus placement exists for this arrangement; heuristic proposes 3 (score 4.475), raised by the left hand's chords
pieces.notes: The first violins' theme (bars 1-16), played softly the second time and ending with the famous fortissimo chord, here in the left hand. First published in 1795 (Offenbach: André, according to IMSLP).

reference.description: Score in the article, section 'II. Andante', first violins bars 1-16, C major

pieces.title: Lullaby (Wiegenlied)
pieces.tempoSource: editorial: Brahms marks 'Zart bewegt' (tenderly moving) without a metronome mark; quarter = 72
pieces.levelNote: Level 2: right hand single notes moving between F4 and F5 in F major; left hand waltz bass, a bass note and a two-note chord; no published syllabus placement exists for this arrangement; heuristic proposes 3 (score 4.81), raised by the waltz chords (chord share 0.67)
pieces.notes: Arranged in F major (the song is in E-flat major). First published by Simrock in November 1868 (IMSLP).

reference.description: Score in the article (section 'Melody'), E-flat major; matches the voice of the Mutopia engraving BrahmsJ/O49/Wiegenlied (Mutopia 1037)

pieces.title: Eine kleine Nachtmusik, opening theme
pieces.catalogue: Serenade in G major, K. 525, 1st movement (opening)
pieces.tempoSource: editorial: Mozart marks Allegro; quarter = 120, a little slower than the usual concert tempo
pieces.levelNote: Level 2: right hand the broken-chord theme from D4 to D5 in G major, moving positions; left hand half notes; no published syllabus placement exists for this arrangement; heuristic proposes 2 (score 2.06)
pieces.notes: The four opening bars of the first movement, an octave lower than the violins. First published about 1827 (Offenbach: André, according to IMSLP).

reference.description: First score in the article, section 'I. Allegro', bars 1-4, G major

rejected.reason: A level-rule failure that a simpler accompaniment cannot fix: the top line of the right hand in the A strain (Mutopia JoplinS/maple, id 23, the reference the plan names; bars 1-16 read from the mirror's LilyPond source) spans 25 semitones, G4 in bar 1 to A-flat 6 in bars 8 to 10, and a level-2 right hand may span 19. The other reading of the melody line, the lowest right-hand note per onset, spans 29 semitones (E-flat 4 to A-flat 6), and an 8-bar half of the strain is either the opening without its answer or the answer without the opening. Replaced by the spare in-the-good-old-summertime.
